correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the all-parameter argument. The truncation crosses no edge interior: the only excluded hypersimplex vertex is H, and all its neighbors lie on the truncating hyperplane. Each original coordinate facet contains a vertex with exactly two outside elements and the requisite fixed coordinate, so its relative interior survives. Inside the new simplex-product facet a face with index sets I,J has the signed coordinate normals on H minus I and O minus J plus the new normal, and one additional coordinate ray for each singleton factor. When both factors have size at least two, omit one coordinate in J to represent the quotient lattice and use an unused I coordinate as a unit pivot for the new ray. A singleton factor gives a dependence among genuine extremal rays, hence nonsimpliciality; this applies also when both factors are singletons. Off the new facet, positive-dimensional faces omit at least two coordinate normals and are unimodular; old vertices have n rays in rank n−1. Maximal nonsmooth faces are the listed simplices and the old vertices. Orbit closures preserve face inclusion and meet along common faces (the word 'reverses' in Proof Step 4 is a prose slip; its displayed equivalence is correct). The simplex difference lattices are saturated. At a maximal singleton-factor face the transverse saturated character lattice identifies with the signed H coordinates (or signed O coordinates), giving independent generators (e_i,0) and (e_i,1) with the only needed exchanges the two-by-two minors. At an old vertex the character semigroup consists of balanced nonnegative margins generated by elementary transfers with the same determinantal exchanges. The Segre degrees give the stated multiplicities. The component count and K_{3,3} example follow, and smooth versus nonsimplicial exhausts the fan, proving the non-Q-factorial statement.
residual_risks: The checker is a bounded face and lattice test, not a proof for all parameters or of the semigroup presentations. No assertion about the nonreduced Jacobian scheme or germs at component crossings was assessed.

value.rationale: Deleting one basis is a natural minimal perturbation of the uniform matroid. The result determines exactly where deleting it replaces isolated hypersimplex singularities with positive-dimensional components, how these meet, and which transverse local rings and multiplicities occur for all rank and corank. This distinguishes local geometry that neither fixed-point class groups nor aggregate face counts resolve.
